results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 68 body units' outline summaries match the controlling idea of their aligned spec paragraph, in spec order (p01-p69; the spec has no p22). The five introduction callouts match no spec paragraph and are mapped to null. p38's 'Versions 4 to 7 are Femke's edits' now sits in the p37 unit, but p38's controlling idea (what the stream does not do) is what its unit and summary carry.

Only Introduction ¶3 was marked two_ideas (place in Part VII and ownership / roadmap). Spec p03 deliberately combines placement, scope boundaries and the roadmap sentence (roadmap placement: 'the closing sentence of p03'), so the unit carries its one declared controlling idea.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: intro, scene and concepts to S1; outbox, CDC and translator to S2; envelope, catalog, topics and the Concepts ordering bullets to S3; removal SLO, schema evolution and replay to S4; public evidence, contract v1, the bike and the Golf to S5; trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, questions and conclusion to S6.

Every table, Figures 1-4 and every quotation (Fowler, Debezium, Kleinanzeigen, domain model, Adevinta, Vinted, Google) is introduced or followed by a sentence or caption saying what it shows. The mechanism table now has 'The table compares the options.' after the conclusion 'CDC and outbox are therefore stages, not alternatives', and its bold rows and 'When it is right' column state the conclusion. The Vinted 2023 and Adevinta Spain bullets carry no own lesson sentence but are framed by 'What is documented is the plumbing around them', and Vinted 2023 is interpreted later in Replay.

Every other section, paragraph, introduction and conclusion boundary expresses its declared relationship and picks up the declared known information (e.g. 'Ingrid's question needs precise terms', 'These concepts become an architecture', 'Where the public record stops at the plumbing', 'Contract v1's fourth decision, full transitive compatibility, follows from one fact', 'Each of those failures needs an owner'). Plain openers at sequence boundaries are carried by subheadings.

Both flow readers stumbled on this sentence.

Both readers describe the declared order (problem/incident -> concepts -> architecture -> evidence and contract v1 -> schema evolution and replay as disciplines over time -> judging sections) and give a reason for every section's position; neither marks a section unclear, and both say the major section order is sound. Points dismissed as not material for the declared audience: Common Ground (A2), Daan Visser (A3/B2), the Essen Golf (A11/B8), the Lyon apartment and entity-resolution cluster (A13/B10), Solr and Safe Deal (B minor) are all on audience.already_knows (cast, programs, recurring examples and earlier chapters); 'First, others' evidence.' Opens on a concrete fan-out example, states the claim, places the chapter in Part VII and its neighbours; no placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report. The roadmap sentence is required by the spec and follows substance.
No bare restatement, grab bag or new subtopic: it synthesizes the two halves, calls back to the hook and the bike, gives a course of action and hands off to listing-data-management.

States what no single section states (producer half and consumer half only work together, as the bike needed both) and why it matters ('catch backfill and schema-change failures before buyers do, and let a new consumer start without asking the producer'), with the takeaway 'Review the next event design by asking which half it lacks.'

'A listing written once and read by ten or twenty systems' returns to the hook, and 'Femke's bike needed both: an event the digest heard, and a digest that re-checked when it sent' returns to the scene, as callback.how declares.

From the opening alone the reader predicted the fan-out framing, one owned published stream, the scope boundaries (copies to listing-data-management, tracking to data-platform), all sections in order (scene, definition, building the stream, testing on engineering posts and docs plus contract v1, schema evolution and replay, trade-offs/verticals/failure modes/Chief Architect's view/questions), the evidence (dated engineering posts from Adevinta, Kleinanzeigen, Vinted, AutoScout24, mobile.de; Confluent and Debezium docs; the fictional Veldmark) and the tone. Unpredicted details (outbox vs CDC recommendation, Kafka) are body content, not omissions from the expected answer.

Digest fix: the digest consumes the owned contract (outbox or CDC plus translator), ListingSold v9 drops the bike, and it re-checks availability at send time. Replay: version-gated apply, events carrying full public state, replay from the compacted listing.state.v1 where closed listings are tombstoned, backfills on a separate version-gated topic. Matches expected.

Names the dual-write failure (crash between commit and publish; forgotten publisher), the transactional outbox and its cost (write-path change, extra table, at-least-once), raw CDC making the internal schema a public contract, and CDC behind a translator/ACL until the new service publishes the same contract through its outbox, with its cost. Matches expected.

Rename: add new field, populate both, deprecate, remove in v2 via a parallel listing.events.v2 topic; the registry under FULL_TRANSITIVE stops an in-place rename. Meaning change: never in place, new field with a new name, passes the registry (syntax not semantics), caught by the forum's one-week event-catalog review. Matches expected.

No real company's listing event names, topics or consumer logic are presented as fact; the draft states that no classifieds company in the research published its listing event names or topic layout; Adevinta, Kleinanzeigen, Vinted, Adevinta Spain, AutoScout24 and mobile.de appear only through dated posts and docs; 2018 and 2022 are flagged as older in the body and 2019 in Sources; the Vinted version-check point is labeled 'my inference'.
